newsitem.title: TURKEY: WGC sees Turkish gold demand at 130 T in 1996.
newsitem.headline: WGC sees Turkish gold demand at 130 T in 1996.

text.p: Turkey's gold demand is expected to pick up to 130 tonnes in the whole of this year from 112.5 tonnes last year and 38 tonnes in 1994, the World Gold Council (WGC) said on Wednesday.
Murat Akman, regional director of the institution, told a two-day International Gold Markets conference in Istanbul a rise in local consumption was the main reason behind the demand surge this year.
Turkey's demand was 25.1 tonnes in the first quarter of 1996, down from 31.7 tonnes in the last 1995 quarter and compared with 11 tonnes in first quarter last year.
Demand peaked in 1993 when it stood at 162.9 tonnes, according to official figures.
